patient.chief_complaint: Sudden bilateral thigh pain on postoperative day 11 after L1-L5 laminectomy, followed by rapidly ascending lower extremity weakness and tingling, with absent reflexes.
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. T. is a 78-year-old woman presenting on postoperative day 11 after an uncomplicated L1-L5 laminectomy with L4/5 posterolateral fusion performed for lumbar spinal stenosis and spondylolisthesis. She had been ambulating with a walker and was progressing appropriately until postoperative day 9, when she had a single episode of loose stool without systemic symptoms. On postoperative day 11, she experienced sudden severe bilateral thigh pain, followed over the next several hours by ascending weakness and worsening tingling in both lower extremities. By the time of evaluation, she cannot stand or walk. The weakness developed rapidly over 12 hours. She is afebrile and her surgical wound appears to be healing well. The immediate concern is a surgical complication — epidural hematoma, hardware displacement, or infection — all of which must be excluded emergently before attributing the weakness to a systemic neurological condition. The single loose stool episode 2 days prior, while appearing inconsequential, may represent the antecedent GI illness triggering an immune response. The temporal relationship between the GI episode, the 11-day post-surgical state, and the acute ascending neuropathy suggests GBS triggered by the combination of surgical stress and a mild GI illness.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP (post-spinal-surgery trigger, possible mechanical contribution)

differential.key_features: Anatomically restricted distribution and asymmetric pattern; symmetric ascending weakness with areflexia argues against pure mechanical injury.
Spinal MRI required; sensory level and sphincter dysfunction absent here; MRI excludes.
Post-op ICU course increases risk; pattern of CSF dissociation and demyelinating EMG argues for GBS.
Sphincter and saddle anaesthesia absent; not consistent.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain CBC, CMP, HIV, anti-GM1/anti-GQ1b ganglioside antibodies, and stool culture / Campylobacter serology if recent diarrhea
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild leukocytosis / elevated inflammatory markers reflecting antecedent infection; ganglioside antibodies for variant typing; trigger identification (Campylobacter, CMV, EBV, Mycoplasma, HIV)

optimal_actions.action: Order nerve conduction studies and needle EMG (EMG/NCS)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Demyelinating pattern (prolonged DML, conduction block, reduced CV, absent F-waves) consistent with AIDP, or reduced CMAP amplitudes in axonal variants (AMAN/AMSAN)

optimal_actions.action: Perform lumbar puncture for CSF analysis
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Albuminocytologic dissociation — elevated protein with cell count <10/μL; may be normal in the first week of illness

optimal_actions.action: Order bedside respiratory function testing (FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF) and repeat every 4–6 hours
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Baseline and serial FVC, MIP/MEP, NIF; deterioration to FVC <20 mL/kg, MIP worse than -30 cmH2O, or VC <40% predicted triggers ICU transfer / intubation

optimal_actions.action: Search the medical literature for IVIG vs plasma exchange evidence to guide disease-modifying therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: IVIG (0.4 g/kg/day x 5 days) and plasma exchange are equivalently effective first-line therapies; combination not superior

optimal_actions.action: Check drug interactions / contraindications for IVIG (renal function, IgA deficiency screen) and/or plasma exchange (coagulation, calcium, hemodynamics)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmation that IVIG can be given safely (no severe renal impairment, no IgA deficiency) or that plasma exchange is appropriate (adequate vascular access, stable coagulation)

optimal_actions.action: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus tachycardia or bradycardia; conduction or repolarisation abnormalities reflecting autonomic involvement

optimal_actions.action: Initiate continuous cardiac telemetry for the first 1–2 weeks for moderate/severe disease — autonomic instability (bradyarrhythmias, BP lability) is common
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Documentation of sinus pauses, bradyarrhythmias, BP lability, or non-sustained tachyarrhythmias

useless_tools.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

sequence_constraints.reason: Document respiratory status (FVC/NIF) before committing to IVIG vs plasma exchange — severe respiratory compromise mandates ICU triage and may influence treatment choice and timing.
Renal function, IgA screen, and CBC must be reviewed before IVIG to mitigate renal failure, anaphylaxis (IgA-deficient patients), and aseptic meningitis risk.

critical_actions: MRI spine to exclude epidural haematoma, residual compression, or operative complication.
Coordinate with surgical team for post-op review.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start corticosteroids as monotherapy.
key_reasoning_points: Surgery is a recognised immune-trigger for GBS; mechanical injury alone is restricted in distribution and timing.
Imaging rules out structural / surgical complication; GBS is diagnosed by Brighton-level clinical and laboratory criteria.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on mechanical / surgical injury rather than autoimmune polyradiculoneuropathy.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Symmetric ascending paralysis with CSF dissociation and demyelinating EMG indicates GBS triggered by the surgical inflammatory milieu, not direct surgical injury.

Agents calling order_specialized_test{respiratory_function} will hit the EMG/NCS output instead. Recommend adding a respiratory_function followup keyed to order_specialized_test in a follow-up case-body pass.
